title: Aukhi Ghari Na Dekhan Dei
subtitle: Apna Birad Samale — He does not let His own see the hard hour
theme: A shabad for hard times, protection and trust
intention: Sing this in the middle of a hard stretch: a hospital wait, an exam result, a night that will not end. Guru Arjan Dev Ji's promise is that the One who protects His own holds out a hand with every breath.
translation_note: English renderings are MedRise Gurbani's own, written for readers new to Gurbani.
arrangement_note: MedRise Gurbani sings it as an uplifting kirtan with the first line as the refrain, so the promise keeps coming back.

verses.g: ਅਉਖੀ ਘੜੀ ਨ ਦੇਖਣ ਦੇਈ ਅਪਨਾ ਬਿਰਦੁ ਸਮਾਲੇ ॥
verses.h: अउखी घड़ी न देखण देई अपना बिरदु समाले ॥
verses.t: Aukhee gharee na dhekhan dheiee apanaa biradh samaale.
verses.e: He does not let His own see a hard hour; He keeps to His age-old nature of caring for them.
verses.s: No deja que los suyos vean una hora difícil; Él cumple su antigua naturaleza de cuidarlos.

verses.g: ਹਾਥ ਦੇਇ ਰਾਖੈ ਅਪਨੇ ਕਉ ਸਾਸਿ ਸਾਸਿ ਪ੍ਰਤਿਪਾਲੇ ॥੧॥
verses.h: हाथ देइ राखै अपने कउ सासि सासि प्रतिपाले ॥१॥
verses.t: Haath dhei raakhai apane kau saas saas pratipaale. ||1||
verses.e: Giving His own hand, He shields His own and sustains them with every breath. ||1||
verses.s: Dándoles su propia mano, protege a los suyos y los sostiene en cada respiración. ||1||

verses.g: ਪ੍ਰਭ ਸਿਉ ਲਾਗਿ ਰਹਿਓ ਮੇਰਾ ਚੀਤੁ ॥
verses.h: प्रभ सिउ लागि रहिओ मेरा चीतु ॥
verses.t: Prabh siau laag rahio meraa cheet.
verses.e: My mind stays attached to God.
verses.s: Mi mente permanece unida a Dios.

verses.g: ਆਦਿ ਅੰਤਿ ਪ੍ਰਭੁ ਸਦਾ ਸਹਾਈ ਧੰਨੁ ਹਮਾਰਾ ਮੀਤੁ ॥ ਰਹਾਉ ॥
verses.h: आदि अंति प्रभु सदा सहाई धंनु हमारा मीतु ॥ रहाउ ॥
verses.t: Aadh ant prabh sadhaa sahaaee dhann hamaaraa meet. || Rahaau ||
verses.e: From beginning to end, God is always my help; blessed is my Friend. || Pause ||
verses.s: Del principio al fin, Dios siempre es mi ayuda; bendito es mi Amigo. || Pausa ||

verses.g: ਮਨਿ ਬਿਲਾਸ ਭਏ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਕੇ ਅਚਰਜ ਦੇਖਿ ਬਡਾਈ ॥
verses.h: मनि बिलास भए साहिब के अचरज देखि बडाई ॥
verses.t: Man bilaas bhe saahib ke acharaj dhekh baddaaee.
verses.e: Seeing the Master's wondrous greatness, my mind is filled with joy.
verses.s: Al ver la maravillosa grandeza del Señor, mi mente se llena de alegría.

verses.g: ਹਰਿ ਸਿਮਰਿ ਸਿਮਰਿ ਆਨਦ ਕਰਿ ਨਾਨਕ ਪ੍ਰਭਿ ਪੂਰਨ ਪੈਜ ਰਖਾਈ ॥੨॥੧੫॥੪੬॥
verses.h: हरि सिमरि सिमरि आनद करि नानक प्रभि पूरन पैज रखाई ॥२॥१५॥४६॥
verses.t: Har simar simar aanadh kar Naanak prabh pooran paij rakhaaee. ||2||15||46||
verses.e: Remember the Lord again and again and live in bliss, O Nanak; God has kept His servant's honor in full. ||2||15||46||
verses.s: Recuerda al Señor una y otra vez y vive en dicha, oh Nanak; Dios ha guardado por completo el honor de su servidor. ||2||15||46||

meaning: “Aukhi Ghari Na Dekhan Dei” (ਅਉਖੀ ਘੜੀ ਨ ਦੇਖਣ ਦੇਈ) means “He does not let His own see a hard hour.” Aukhi is hard or painful, ghari is a moment or an hour, and birad is God's innate, age-old nature of caring for those who are His. The next line makes the promise physical: God gives His own hand and sustains His devotee with every breath (saas saas).

The shabad is by Guru Arjan Dev Ji in Raag Dhanasari, on Ang 682 of Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji. Its Rahao, the line the whole shabad turns on, is “Prabh siau laag rahio meraa cheet”: my mind stays attached to God, the Friend who helps from beginning to end. It closes with Guru Ji's own conclusion: remember the Lord again and again and live in bliss, because God has kept His servant's honor in full.

Sangats sing it through hard stretches such as illness, exams, money worries or a long wait for news, and in thanks once they have passed. MedRise Gurbani offers it as a shabad for hard times: a reminder that you are held, breath by breath.
faq: What does “Aukhi Ghari Na Dekhan Dei” mean?
It means “He does not let His own see a hard hour.” The line continues “apanaa biradh samaale”: God keeps to His age-old nature of protecting those who are His.
Who wrote Aukhi Ghari Na Dekhan Dei and where is it in Gurbani?
Guru Arjan Dev Ji, the fifth Sikh Guru. It is in Raag Dhanasari (Dhanasari Mahalla 5) on Ang 682 of Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji.
Is it spelled ਅਉਖੀ or ਔਖੀ?
Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji spells it ਅਉਖੀ. ਔਖੀ is the modern Punjabi spelling of the same word, and both are said “aukhi.” This page shows the Gurbani spelling.
What is the Rahao line of this shabad?
“Prabh siau laag rahio meraa cheet, aadh ant prabh sadhaa sahaaee dhann hamaaraa meet”: my mind stays attached to God; from beginning to end God is always my help; blessed is my Friend.
It is a common kirtan shabad for difficult times and for giving thanks once a hard time has passed. Many kirtan recordings sing the first line as the refrain.
